findings.message:
NEW this run, and introduced BY the run-005 repair. RRQ-05 asks candidates to explain a claim the unit does not teach and its own taught text contradicts. `assessment` fails on this item alone.

Stem, docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-04/unit-assessment.mdx:133-134:
  "Describe the three-level architecture of Pakistan's National Professional Standards, and
   explain why only the performance level yields indicators an observer can check. *(Understand)*"
Mark scheme, unit-assessment.mdx:227-230:
  "Ten standards (1); each divided into knowledge, dispositions, performance (2); explains that
   knowledge and dispositions are inferred from what performance shows, so only the performance
   level states something an observer can watch for (1); indicators beneath, stating observably
   what meeting a part looks like (1)."

Three independent problems.

1. THE CLAIM IS NEVER TAUGHT. Grepping all four topic files for `infer`, `performance level`,
   `only the performance` and `watch for` returns nothing. Those strings occur ONLY at
   unit-assessment.mdx:134 and :228-229. The nearest thing in the unit is topic-02.mdx:211-213,
   "Most trainees discover that the dispositions part is nearly impossible to evidence by
   watching" - which is about dispositions only, about observation only, and is framed as a
   practicum discovery rather than a property of the architecture. Nothing anywhere in the unit
   addresses whether the knowledge level is observable.

2. THE TAUGHT TEXT CONTRADICTS IT. topic-02.mdx:64-66: "**Indicators.** Beneath the parts sit
   indicators: specific, observable statements of what meeting that part looks like in practice."
   Restated at topic-02.mdx:179-181 and again in the assessment's own Unit summary at
   unit-assessment.mdx:31-34. "The parts" is plural and covers knowledge and dispositions, so on
   the account the unit actually teaches, observable indicators exist for all three parts. A
   candidate who studied the unit cannot answer this item correctly.

3. THE MARK SCHEME CONTRADICTS ITSELF. Its third point ("only the performance level states
   something an observer can watch for") and its fourth ("indicators beneath, stating observably
   what meeting a part looks like") cannot both hold. A candidate answering from the taught text
   loses mark 3 and earns mark 4; one answering as the stem presupposes does the reverse. This is
   a conflicting criterion in the sense of references/g3.md, "Flag conflicting keys and criteria".

Corroborating, not itself the defect: fig-U4-3's prompt and alt text
(specs/content/efmp-302/figures/unit-04.md; carried at topic-02.mdx:24) place indicators "beneath
the performance band" only, so the figure and the prose already disagree, which is plausibly where
the stem's premise came from. And specs/content/efmp-302/concepts/unit-04.md maps RRQ-05 to
CON:EFMP-302-4-7, -4-8 and -4-9 but NOT to CON:EFMP-302-4-10 (Indicator), so the derived concept
mapping does not cover what the rewritten stem now asks.

TWO DEFENSIBLE REMEDIES; THE CHOICE IS THE OWNER'S, NOT THE REVIEWER'S.
(a) Reword the added clause so the item asks something the unit establishes. Note that the
    obvious candidate, "explain what the three-part division buys", duplicates RRQ-06
    (unit-assessment.mdx:139-140), so this needs care rather than a one-line swap.
(b) Keep the clause and make the claim true: amend topic-02.mdx:64-66 and fig-U4-3 so the
    architecture really does attach indicators to the performance level, and say how knowledge and
    dispositions are evidenced instead. This changes taught prose and a committed SVG plus its
    dark variant, and would require re-running check:figures and figures:variants:check.
